parsed.modern: the ell of Venice. At Goa, and other parts, they use a larger cando, equal to fifteen Dutch ells; exceeding that of Babel and Balfora by 2 per centum, and the vera by 6 1/2. In Siam, they use the ken, short of three Paris feet by one inch. The ken contains two foks, the fok two keubs, the keub twelve minor or inches, the niou to be equal to eight grains of rice, i. e. to about nine lines. At Cambioa, they use the hafter; in Japan, the tatam; and the span on some of the coasts of Guinea.
